title: Tourists Evacuated by Boat as Wildfires Sweep Greek and Croatian Resorts
excerpt: More than 300 people fled by sea from a Greek beach town as Europe faces what the EU calls very extreme wildfire conditions from record heat.
body:
• More than 300 tourists and residents were evacuated by boat from the Greek seaside town of Siviri as wildfire engulfed forests in the Halkidiki region
  • In Croatia, a wildfire near the resort town of Omis killed one person, injured 40, and forced 1,200 to evacuate
  • Wildfires driven by record heat and drought are burning across Spain, France, England, and the Balkans in what the EU calls 'very extreme' conditions
  • Greece has already seen major fire evacuations this summer, including 2,000 tourists rescued from Crete in late July

Tourists and residents fled seaside resorts across southern Europe by land and sea this week as wildfires fanned by scorching heat and fierce winds tore through Greece, Croatia, France, and Spain during the peak holiday season.

In northern Greece, dramatic scenes unfolded in the seaside town of Siviri on the Halkidiki peninsula, where people wearing face masks, some clutching children or pets, boarded dinghies and fishing boats as fire consumed surrounding forests and columns of smoke turned the sky dark grey, according to Reuters.

Rescue Operations at Sea

The Greek coast guard evacuated more than 300 people by boat from Siviri, a picturesque town of woodland, olive groves, and beaches located south of Thessaloniki, the country's second-largest city. Patrol boats, fire boats, and fishing vessels all participated in the operation.

As the blaze approached from inland, flames charred holiday apartments and their sea-facing balconies. More than 140 firefighters, nine aircraft, and seven helicopters were deployed to battle flames raging on both sides of the main road from Siviri to Kassandreia. One firefighter was injured.

"Our effort is focused on extinguishing the fire and the safe transport of people."

— Giannis Artopios, Greek Fire Brigade Spokesman

Deadly Blaze on Croatia's Dalmatian Coast

Overnight, a wildfire engulfed homes near Omis, a scenic town on Croatia's prized Dalmatian coast, killing one person and injuring 40, seven of them seriously. Roughly 1,200 people were evacuated as flames turned the night sky red, according to Reuters.

"The flames were licking both sides of the road. When I got a little further around the bend and looked, I saw flames shooting up from under my hood. The car was on fire!" said local resident Ljubica Uglesic, describing her escape.

A Continent on Fire

The wildfires are not isolated to the eastern Mediterranean. In southwestern France, authorities evacuated 525 people from the village of Luglon in the Landes region, near an area already devastated by major blazes this summer. In southern Spain, a fire in Huelva has burned 31,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 700 people. Spanish firefighting planes have logged more than 8,200 hours of flight time this year, already exceeding the total for 2025, when a record 393,000 hectares burned.

In England, a grass fire in Stourbridge spread across a golf course and reached residential areas. "I heard a scream, and all the trees along the railway track were exploding," said local resident Paul Nash, whose neighbor's house burned down.

Climate Crisis Driving Extreme Conditions

The European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service warned of "very extreme" wildfire conditions stretching across central and eastern Europe, with additional pockets over southern Britain, Ireland, northern France, and southern Sweden through August 19.

Average high temperatures across Western Europe on Friday were forecast at 31.2°C (88°F) — 8°C above the 1961-1990 average. Successive heatwaves since May have intensified drought, strained water supplies, and left vegetation tinder-dry across the continent.

What Travelers Should Know

Greece has been hit particularly hard this summer. In late July, about 2,000 tourists were evacuated from Crete, where fires destroyed hotels and farmland. Two firefighters died battling those blazes. Earlier fires forced 500 people to flee by boat from coastal Boeotia. More than 70 fires broke out across Greece on a single day in late July.

The hot, dry conditions are expected to persist. For travelers planning Mediterranean holidays, the fires underscore the growing risk that climate-driven extreme weather poses to popular European destinations. Travel advisories for fire-affected regions in Greece, Croatia, Spain, and France remain in effect, and authorities are urging tourists to monitor local warnings closely.
